# Authentication & Credential Management Procedure

## Purpose

This procedure operationalizes Example Org's identification, authentication, and credential management controls so that every account, device, and session accessing Example Org systems is uniquely identified, appropriately authenticated, and continuously protected against credential compromise.

## Scope

This procedure applies to IAM Engineering staff and any delegated system administrators who configure authentication, session, and credential controls on all Example Org information systems, including systems processing electronic protected health information (ePHI) and systems accessed by organizational, non-organizational, and non-privileged/privileged users. It runs on a continuous basis as accounts, devices, and credentials are provisioned, used, and retired.

## Prerequisites

- Administrative access to the [Identity Provider] console and its authentication policy engine
- Access to a [Ticketing System] for logging exceptions, lockout overrides, and remediation actions
- Access to a [Mobile Device Management Platform] for mobile purge/wipe configuration
- Access to a [Configuration Management Database] or configuration baseline scanning tool
- Access to a [Password Manager] platform approved for organizational use
- Access to [Public Key Infrastructure] management tooling and trust store consoles
- Access to a [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform] for policy/documentation retention
- Current approved Authentication & Credential Management Standard and applicable Security and Privacy Plan(s) (SSPP)
- Written approval from the [System Owner] or [Chief Information Security Officer] for any control exception
- Baseline reporting capability to generate the MFA enrolment report and Authentication policy configuration export

## Procedure Steps

### Invalid Logon Attempt Limiting [NIST AC-7 | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] console, configure the account lockout policy to trigger after 5 consecutive invalid logon attempts within a 15-minute window.
1. Set the automatic response to lock the account for a minimum of 30 minutes or until an administrator releases it; disable automatic time-based unlock unless a documented operational exception exists.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to notify IAM Engineering via the [Ticketing System] whenever a lockout event fires.
1. Where an operational exception to manual release is required, document the justification and route it to the [System Owner] for approval before implementing an alternate unlock method.
1. Log all lockout and override events; include lockout configuration state in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Mobile Device Purge on Failed Logon [NIST AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7(2) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Mobile Device Management Platform], configure the device wipe/purge trigger to activate after 10 consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts.
1. Define and apply the approved purge/wipe technique (full device wipe or container wipe) per the organization's mobile device configuration profile.
1. Verify the purge policy is applied to all enrolled devices via a compliance scan in the [Mobile Device Management Platform].
1. Capture the applied purge configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Biometric Logon Attempt Limiting [NIST AC-7(3)]

1. Identify all systems using biometric logon in the [Identity Provider] or endpoint biometric subsystem.
1. Set the maximum consecutive unsuccessful biometric attempts to [Biometric Attempt Limit] in the applicable configuration console.
1. Confirm the limit triggers the same automatic response defined for invalid logon attempts (lockout/notification).
1. Record the configured value in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Alternate Authentication Factors After Lockout [NIST AC-7(4)]

1. If alternate factors are approved for use after the primary invalid-attempt threshold is exceeded, configure them in the [Identity Provider] (e.g., a secondary verification method).
1. Set a separate consecutive invalid-attempt limit for the alternate factor within [Alternate Factor Attempt Window] and configure automatic lockout/notification on exceeding it.
1. Document which accounts/services are permitted to use alternate factors in the applicable SSPP.

### System Use Notification Banner [NIST AC-8 | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

1. Configure the pre-authentication banner on all in-scope systems to display: (a) notice that the system is a U.S. Government system or contains U.S. Government information, (b) notice that usage may be monitored, recorded, and audited, (c) notice that unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal/civil penalty, and (d) notice that continued use constitutes consent to monitoring.
1. Configure the banner to remain on screen until the user takes explicit action (e.g., clicks "I Agree" or presses a defined key) to proceed to logon.
1. For publicly accessible systems, configure a banner variant that includes only the applicable monitoring/recording references and a description of authorized uses, displayed under the conditions defined for that system.
1. Work with the [System Owner] to determine which systems in the environment require the banner and record that determination in the applicable SSPP.
1. If compliance is not verified through configuration baseline checks, document in a written agreement how verification results will be produced and their periodicity, and store the agreement in the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].

### Concurrent Session Limiting [NIST AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider], set the concurrent session limit to one (1) session per account and per account type by default.
1. For any account/account type requiring more than one concurrent session, document the justification in the applicable security and privacy plan and obtain [System Owner] approval before configuring the exception.
1. Verify the concurrent session setting during each configuration export and include it in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Device Lock on Inactivity [NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | NIST AC-11(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

1. Configure endpoint and session policies (via the [Identity Provider] or endpoint management tool) to initiate a device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity, applied to both remote and internal connections.
1. Enable the manual lock option so users can initiate a lock before stepping away.
1. Configure the lock screen to display a publicly viewable image that conceals all previously visible content.
1. Configure the lock to remain in effect until the user re-authenticates through the established identification and authentication procedure.
1. Verify the inactivity timeout and lock-screen configuration in the periodic configuration export.

### Workstation Use Policies for ePHI Access [HIPAA 164.310(b)]

1. IAM Engineering, in coordination with the [System Owner], documents the approved functions, manner of use, and physical placement/attributes for each workstation or workstation class permitted to access ePHI.
1. Publish the workstation policy to affected personnel via the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].
1. Review workstation configurations against the documented policy during routine compliance scans.

### Automatic Session Termination [NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii)]

1. Define the triggering conditions for automatic session termination (inactivity period, incident response action, time-of-day restriction) in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] or application session manager to terminate sessions automatically when a defined condition occurs, including terminating electronic sessions after the configured period of inactivity.
1. Test termination behavior for each configured trigger and record results in the [Ticketing System].

### User-Initiated Logout Capability [NIST AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]

1. Identify the information resources requiring authenticated access and record them in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure a visible, user-accessible logout control for every communications session to those resources.
1. Verify logout functionality terminates the session and associated tokens immediately upon activation.

### Explicit Logout Message [NIST AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]

1. Configure the session termination flow to display the standard logout message "Your session has been terminated" upon logout.
1. Document this standard message text in the applicable SSPP.
1. Confirm the message renders correctly across supported client platforms.

### Session Expiration Warning [NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]

1. Define the warning lead time (the period before termination at which the warning displays) in the applicable SSPP as [Session Expiration Warning Lead Time].
1. Configure the session manager to display an explicit warning message to the user at that lead time before automatic termination.
1. Validate the warning displays correctly in a test session and log the result.

### Technical Access Restriction for ePHI Systems [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]

1. Configure role- and identity-based access controls in the [Identity Provider] so that only authorized persons and authorized software programs can reach systems containing ePHI.
1. Review and reconcile the access control list against the current authorization roster on a continuous basis.
1. Remove or adjust access immediately upon identification of any unauthorized entry via the [Ticketing System].

### Unique User Identification [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i)]

1. Assign each user a unique username and/or numeric identifier in the [Identity Provider] at account creation; prohibit reuse of identifiers across users.
1. Confirm the unique identifier is used to track all logon, access, and audit events for that user.
1. Record identifier assignment in the account provisioning record retained in the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].

### Emergency Access Procedure [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii)]

1. Document the emergency access procedure describing how authorized personnel obtain necessary ePHI during an emergency, including the approval chain and the temporary credential/break-glass mechanism used.
1. Configure a break-glass account or emergency access role in the [Identity Provider], subject to enhanced logging and post-use review.
1. Test the emergency access procedure and store test evidence in the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].

### Encryption/Decryption Mechanism for ePHI [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]

1. Determine, in coordination with the [System Owner], whether encryption of ePHI at rest/in transit is reasonable and appropriate for each system; document the risk-based decision.
1. Where implemented, configure the approved encryption mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI transparently to authorized workflows.
1. Record the encryption configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Identification & Authentication Policy Governance [NIST IA-1 | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

1. IAM Engineering drafts and maintains the identification and authentication policy and associated procedures, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and applicable legal/regulatory compliance.
1. Designate the IAM Engineering lead as the official responsible for developing, documenting, and disseminating the policy and procedures to the personnel/roles defined in the organizational SSPP.
1. Disseminate the current policy and procedures to defined personnel via the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].
1. Review and update the policy and procedures at least annually and following defined trigger events (audit findings, security incidents, legal/regulatory changes).
1. Record each review cycle and its outcome in the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].

### Documentation Retention & Maintenance [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

1. Maintain all authentication and credential management policies, procedures, and required action/activity/assessment records in written (which may be electronic) form in the [Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Platform].
1. Retain each document for 6 years from the date of creation or last effective date, whichever is later.
1. Make current documentation available to all personnel responsible for implementing the related procedures.
1. Review documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting security; log each review.

### Unique Identification & Authentication of Organizational Users [NIST IA-2 | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(d)]

1. Provision every organizational user (and any process acting on their behalf) with a unique identity in the [Identity Provider] before granting any local, network, or remote access.
1. Configure identity proofing and authentication workflows to comply with the current NIST SP 800-63 suite.
1. Require unique authenticators for each identity; document any authorized exception involving a shared group authenticator and its compensating controls in the applicable SSPP.
1. Require positive user identification (e.g., unique identifier verification) for any help desk transaction with security or privacy implications.
1. Include current enrollment status in the MFA enrolment report to confirm unique identity binding.

### Multi-Factor Authentication for Privileged Accounts [NIST IA-2(1) | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider], enforce MFA using two or more distinct factor types (something you know/have/are) for every privileged account, regardless of local, network, or remote access path.
1. Configure the MFA method to be phishing-resistant per current CISA guidance.
1. Generate the MFA enrolment report on a continuous basis and remediate any privileged account found without compliant MFA via the [Ticketing System].

### Multi-Factor Authentication for Non-Privileged Accounts [NIST IA-2(2) | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

1. Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all non-privileged organizational account types in the [Identity Provider].
1. For consumer-facing accounts, strongly encourage MFA enrollment through in-product prompts even where not yet mandatory.
1. Track enrollment status in the MFA enrolment report and follow up on non-enrolled accounts through the [Ticketing System].

### Individual Authentication for Shared Accounts [NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

1. Where a shared account or authenticator exists, require each individual user to authenticate with their own unique credential in the [Identity Provider] before the system grants access to the shared resource.
1. Log the individual identity behind every shared-account session for audit purposes.
1. Periodically confirm no shared account permits access without preceding individual authentication.

### Separate-Device MFA Factor [NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]

1. Configure at least one MFA factor for both privileged and non-privileged accounts to originate from a device separate from the system being accessed (e.g., hardware token, authenticator app on a separate mobile device).
1. Verify the separate device meets the current published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography standard.
1. Apply this requirement uniformly to local, network, and remote access paths.
1. Record the separate-device factor type in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Replay-Resistant Authentication [NIST IA-2(8) | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

1. Configure authentication protocols for privileged and non-privileged account access to use replay-resistant mechanisms (e.g., time-based one-time passwords, cryptographic nonces, challenge-response).
1. Validate protocol configuration in the [Identity Provider] rejects replayed authentication attempts during a test.
1. Document the configured mechanism in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Single Sign-On [NIST IA-2(10)]

1. Identify the system accounts and services designated for single sign-on (SSO) in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] as the SSO authority for those accounts/services using an approved federation protocol.
1. Validate that SSO sessions inherit the applicable MFA, session timeout, and lockout controls defined elsewhere in this procedure.

### PIV Credential Acceptance [NIST IA-2(12)]

1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials for applicable users.
1. Validate the PIV certificate chain and revocation status during each verification event.
1. Log PIV verification outcomes for audit review.

### Out-of-Band Authentication [NIST IA-2(13)]

1. Define the conditions under which out-of-band authentication (e.g., a call-back or secondary channel confirmation) is required, in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure the out-of-band mechanism in the [Identity Provider] to trigger under those defined conditions.
1. Test the out-of-band flow and log results in the [Ticketing System].

### Device Identification & Authentication [NIST IA-3 Moderate/High | NIST IA-3(1) | NIST IA-3(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

1. Maintain a documented list of approved device types permitted to connect locally, remotely, or over the network, recorded in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure network access control lists using, at minimum, MAC or IP address-based shared information to identify and authenticate approved devices before connection.
1. Where cryptographically based bidirectional device authentication is required, configure mutual certificate-based authentication between device and system prior to connection establishment.
1. Where attestation-based identification is used instead, verify the device's configuration state through the defined configuration management process before granting connection.
1. Record device authentication method and approved device list version in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Dynamic Address Allocation Lease Management [NIST IA-3(3)]

1. Configure the DHCP or address-allocation service to apply standardized lease information and lease duration per the defined organizational requirements.
1. Configure audit logging so that lease assignment to a device is recorded at time of assignment.
1. Review lease audit logs on a continuous basis for anomalies.

### Authenticator Management [NIST IA-5 | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

1. Verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device before issuing an authenticator, using the identity proofing process defined for IA-2/IA-8.
1. Establish initial authenticator content and confirm it meets the strength-of-mechanism requirement for its intended use.
1. Follow documented administrative procedures in the [Identity Provider] and [Ticketing System] for initial distribution, and for handling lost, compromised, or damaged authenticators, including revocation.
1. Change all default/vendor-supplied authenticators prior to first use of any account or device.
1. Protect authenticator content (secrets, seeds, keys) from unauthorized disclosure or modification using access-restricted storage.
1. Require individuals and devices to implement the protective controls specified in the applicable SSPP (e.g., not sharing credentials, securing hardware tokens).
1. Change the authenticator for any group or role account immediately upon a membership change.

### Authenticator Change/Refresh Schedule [NIST IA-5(f) | FedRAMP IA-5(f) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(f) AE Mandatory]

1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to force an immediate authenticator change upon known or suspected compromise.
1. Configure a forced change of any default or vendor-supplied authenticator immediately upon system installation.
1. Apply the strongly recommended six-month rotation cadence to system and user account passwords where technically enforceable.
1. Log all forced and scheduled authenticator changes in the [Ticketing System].

### FedRAMP Digital Identity Guidelines Compliance [FedRAMP IA-5]

1. Determine the applicable Certification Class for each system (Class B = IAL/AAL/FAL Level 1, Class C = Level 2, Class D = Level 3) and configure the [Identity Provider] accordingly.
1. Configure authentication assertions passed through third parties (e.g., browsers) to be encrypted using XML-Encryption for SAML assertions or JWE for OpenID Connect ID Tokens.
1. Validate assertion encryption configuration during each Authentication policy configuration export.

### NIST SP 800-63B Compliance & Password-MFA Pairing [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

1. Confirm all authenticator management configurations comply with the current published NIST SP 800-63B.
1. Pair all organizational system and user account passwords with MFA consistent with the privileged/non-privileged MFA requirements above.
1. Strongly encourage pairing consumer account passwords with MFA through in-product enrollment prompts.

### Password-Based Authentication Controls [NIST IA-5(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

1. Maintain a list of commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords in the [Identity Provider] or an integrated password-check service; update the list at least annually or immediately upon suspected compromise.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to verify every new or updated password against that list before acceptance.
1. Ensure passwords are transmitted only over cryptographically protected channels (TLS or equivalent) between client and authentication service.
1. Configure password storage to use an approved salted key derivation function, preferably a keyed hash, with salting enabled to mitigate brute-force attacks.
1. Require immediate selection of a new permanent password upon any account recovery; treat any temporary password as requiring an immediate change with no extended lifetime.
1. Allow user selection of long passwords/passphrases including spaces and all printable characters; prohibit dictionary words.
1. Enable an automated strength-assistance tool in the password change workflow to help users select strong passwords.
1. Enforce minimum password length of 8 characters for consumer and all other standard accounts, and 12 characters for administrator/privileged accounts, per the current NIST SP 800-63B composition guidance.
1. Where organizational risk tolerance supports it, document and apply an exclusion of mobile devices from full complexity requirements.

### Public Key-Based Authentication [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate/High]

1. Configure the [Public Key Infrastructure] to enforce authorized access controls on private keys before they can be used for authentication.
1. Map each authenticated identity to the corresponding individual's or group's account in the [Identity Provider].
1. Where PKI is used, validate certificates through a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including a certificate status (revocation) check.
1. Maintain a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation during offline or degraded connectivity.

### Default Authenticator Change by Developers/Installers [NIST IA-5(5)]

1. Require developers and system installers to provide unique authenticators for each deployed component, or to change any default authenticator, prior to delivery and installation.
1. Verify default-authenticator status as part of the pre-deployment acceptance checklist stored in the [Ticketing System].

### Authenticator Protection Commensurate with Security Category [NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]

1. Classify each system's security category per the applicable SSPP.
1. Apply authenticator storage, transmission, and access controls proportionate to that category (e.g., stronger encryption and access restriction for higher-category systems).
1. Document the applied protections in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Prohibition on Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators [NIST IA-5(7) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(7) AE Mandatory]

1. Scan application source code, configuration files, and scripts for embedded unencrypted static authenticators using the organization's code scanning tooling.
1. Remove or encrypt any discovered embedded static authenticator and rotate it immediately.
1. Log the remediation in the [Ticketing System].

### Managing Cross-System Account Risk [NIST IA-5(8)]

1. Identify individuals holding accounts on multiple systems through the [Identity Provider]'s identity correlation report.
1. Apply defined compensating controls (e.g., unique authenticators per system, monitoring for correlated compromise) to those accounts.
1. Review cross-system account risk on a continuous basis.

### Credential Federation with External Organizations [NIST IA-5(9)]

1. Identify the external organizations approved to federate credentials into Example Org systems, per the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure federation trust relationships in the [Identity Provider] only with those approved external organizations.
1. Review the federation partner list periodically and remove any unapproved trust relationship.

### Dynamic Identity/Authenticator Binding [NIST IA-5(10)]

1. Define the binding rules governing how identities are dynamically bound to authenticators, per the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to apply those binding rules automatically at enrollment and re-binding events.
1. Validate binding behavior during periodic configuration review.

### Biometric Quality Requirements [NIST IA-5(12)]

1. Define the required biometric quality thresholds (false match/false non-match rates) applicable to Example Org biometric systems.
1. Configure biometric capture and matching subsystems to enforce those thresholds.
1. Validate configuration compliance during periodic review.

### Cached Authenticator Restrictions [NIST IA-5(13)]

1. Define the maximum permitted cached-authenticator time period as [Cached Authenticator Time Limit].
1. Configure client and server components to purge cached authenticators after that period.
1. Verify cached-credential purge behavior during a configuration test.

### PKI Trust Store Management [NIST IA-5(14)]

1. Establish an organization-wide methodology for managing PKI trust store content across all networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications.
1. Apply the methodology consistently when adding, removing, or updating trusted certificate authorities in each platform's trust store.
1. Record trust store baseline state in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### GSA-Approved ICAM Products [NIST IA-5(15)]

1. Before procuring or configuring any identity, credential, or access management product or service, confirm it appears on the current GSA-approved products/services list.
1. Document the approval verification in the procurement record.

### In-Person/Trusted-Party Authenticator Issuance [NIST IA-5(16)]

1. Define which authenticator types require in-person or trusted-external-party issuance, per the applicable SSPP.
1. Route issuance of those authenticator types through the defined registration authority, requiring authorization by the defined personnel/roles before issuance.
1. Log each issuance event and its authorizer in the [Ticketing System].

### Presentation Attack Detection [NIST IA-5(17)]

1. Enable presentation attack detection (liveness detection) on all biometric authentication mechanisms.
1. Validate detection effectiveness during periodic testing of the biometric subsystem.

### Password Manager Use [NIST IA-5(18)]

1. Designate the approved [Password Manager] platform for organizational password generation and management.
1. Configure the password manager to enforce the protective controls defined for it in the applicable SSPP (e.g., encrypted vault, master authentication with MFA).
1. Require users to store organizational credentials only in the approved password manager.

### Authentication Feedback Obscuring [NIST IA-6 | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

1. Configure all logon interfaces to mask authentication feedback (e.g., display asterisks/dots for typed passwords) so entered credentials are not visible on screen.
1. Where applicable, limit the display time of any temporarily revealed characters.
1. Validate masking behavior on each new or updated logon interface before release.

### Cryptographic Module Authentication [NIST IA-7 | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

1. Configure authentication to cryptographic modules to meet applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.
1. For systems containing PII, configure encryption using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant standard.
1. Record cryptographic module configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Non-Organizational User Identification & Authentication [NIST IA-8 | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

1. Provision non-organizational users (and processes acting on their behalf) with unique identities in the [Identity Provider] before granting access.
1. Configure identity proofing and authentication to comply with the current NIST SP 800-63-3 Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL-2/AAL-2.
1. Require positive identification for any help desk transaction involving a non-organizational user with security or privacy implications.
1. Include non-organizational account enrollment status in the MFA enrolment report.

### PIV Credentials from Other Federal Agencies [NIST IA-8(1)]

1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to accept and electronically verify PIV credentials issued by other federal agencies.
1. Validate the certificate chain and revocation status during each verification.

### External Authenticator Acceptance List [NIST IA-8(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

1. Maintain a documented list of accepted external authenticators, limited to those that are NIST-compliant.
1. For ARC-AMPE-covered systems, confirm each external credential is certified compliant with the current NIST SP 800-63 suite by an approved accreditation authority and meets or exceeds that guidance.
1. Confirm any identity/credential/access management product used for this purpose is GSA-approved.
1. Review and update the accepted-authenticator list periodically.

### Identity Management Profile Conformance [NIST IA-8(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]

1. Define the identity management profiles Example Org conforms to, based on identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the current NIST SP 800-63 suite.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to enforce the defined profiles for applicable user populations.

### Federated/PKI Credential (PIV-I) Acceptance [NIST IA-8(5)]

1. Define the applicable PIV-I policy for accepted federated or PKI credentials.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to accept and verify credentials meeting that policy.

### Identity Attribute Disassociation [NIST IA-8(6)]

1. Define the measures required to disassociate user attributes or identifier-assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties.
1. Configure the federation/identity architecture to apply those disassociation measures for applicable transactions.

### Re-Authentication Triggers [NIST IA-11 | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

1. Define the circumstances requiring re-authentication (role change, authenticator/credential change, system security category change, execution of a privileged function, fixed time period, or periodic interval) in the applicable SSPP.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] or application session manager to force re-authentication automatically when each defined circumstance occurs.
1. At minimum, configure a fixed-time-period re-authentication requirement as defined in the SSPP.
1. Validate re-authentication triggers during periodic testing and log results in the [Ticketing System].

## Roles & Responsibilities

IAM Engineering owns this procedure end to end: it configures, tests, monitors, and maintains all authentication and credential controls described above, and generates the MFA enrolment report and Authentication policy configuration export on a continuous basis. System Owners define which parts of their environment require specific controls (e.g., system use notification scope, in-scope information resources) and document exceptions in the applicable SSPP; the [Chief Information Security Officer] or [System Owner] reviews and approves any deviation from a mandatory control before IAM Engineering implements it.

## Related Standard

Authentication & Credential Management Standard
